deck.title: CloudFormation
deck.analogy: CloudFormation is the written recipe for your infrastructure: console clicking is improvised baking you can't repeat, a template lets AWS cook it identically every time.

subtopics.title: Features → scenarios (this is the exam meat)

cards.front: What is AWS CloudFormation and what is a stack?

back.answer: CloudFormation describes infrastructure in a YAML or JSON template; a running instance of a template is a stack.
back.explanation: This is Infrastructure as Code: templates live in version control and deploy identically to dev/test/prod or new regions.
back.mnemonic: CloudFormation = the written recipe; stack = the cake baked from it.

cards.front: What does CloudFormation do by default if stack creation fails partway?

back.answer: It rolls back automatically by default.
back.explanation: No half-built infrastructure is left behind.
back.mnemonic: No half-baked cakes left in the oven.

cards.front: CloudFormation template: what is the Parameters section for?

back.answer: Inputs supplied at deploy time, such as instance size or environment name.

cards.front: CloudFormation template: what is the Mappings section for?

back.answer: Lookup tables, e.g. the right AMI ID per region.

cards.front: CloudFormation template: what is the Conditions section for?

back.answer: Conditional logic, e.g. "only create this in prod".

cards.front: Which CloudFormation template section is the only required one?
CloudFormation Outputs section: how do stacks share values?

back.answer: Outputs surface values after creation; Export them and another stack reads them with Fn::ImportValue.

cards.front: CloudFormation intrinsic functions: !Ref vs !GetAtt vs !Sub?

back.answer: !Ref references a parameter/resource; !GetAtt grabs a resource attribute; !Sub substitutes variables into a string.
back.explanation: Example of GetAtt: an instance's DNS name.

cards.front: What are CloudFormation Change Sets?

back.answer: A preview of what an update would create/modify/delete before you apply it.

cards.sourceHeading: Features → scenarios (this is the exam meat)

cards.front: What do CloudFormation Stack Policies do?

back.answer: Protect specific resources in a stack from being modified by stack updates.

cards.sourceHeading: Features → scenarios (this is the exam meat)

cards.front: What question does CloudFormation Drift Detection answer?

back.answer: Did someone hand-edit resources in the console? It compares live reality to the template.

cards.sourceHeading: Features → scenarios (this is the exam meat)

cards.front: What are CloudFormation StackSets?

back.answer: Deploy one template to many accounts and regions in one operation.
back.explanation: Use for rolling out a security baseline across an organization.

cards.sourceHeading: Features → scenarios (this is the exam meat)

cards.front: What are CloudFormation Nested Stacks?

back.answer: Stacks inside stacks, packaging common patterns (e.g. a standard VPC) as reusable components.

cards.sourceHeading: Features → scenarios (this is the exam meat)

cards.front: What does CloudFormation DeletionPolicy do, and what are its options?

back.answer: Per-resource instruction on stack deletion: Retain keeps the resource; Snapshot snapshots it first (RDS, EBS, etc.).

cards.sourceHeading: Features → scenarios (this is the exam meat)

cards.front: Trap: what happens when someone manually edits a CloudFormation stack-managed resource in the console?

back.answer: The template isn't updated; it creates drift, and the next stack update can stomp the edit.
back.explanation: Find drift with Drift Detection; prevent it with discipline.

cards.sourceHeading: Features → scenarios (this is the exam meat)

cards.front: What is the AWS CDK relative to CloudFormation?

back.answer: Write infrastructure in Python/TypeScript/Java; it compiles down to CloudFormation templates.
back.explanation: Gives real programming-language loops and logic.

cards.sourceHeading: Features → scenarios (this is the exam meat)

cards.front: Elastic Beanstalk vs CloudFormation: scope?

back.answer: Beanstalk builds the standard web-app stack from your code (using CloudFormation underneath); CloudFormation builds any infrastructure in any shape.
back.mnemonic: Beanstalk = specific meal deal; CloudFormation = whole grocery store.

cards.front: A team must review what changes a CloudFormation template update will make before applying it. What to use?

choices.why: Compares live resources to template, not update preview.
Protects resources from updates, no preview.

cards.front: Deploy standardized security/compliance resources to all accounts in an organization across regions with CloudFormation. What?

choices.why: Componentizes within templates, not multi-account deploy.
Deploys one template across accounts and regions.

cards.front: Ensure the RDS database is not deleted when the CloudFormation stack is torn down. What?

back.answer: DeletionPolicy: Retain (or Snapshot for a final copy).

choices.why: Keeps the resource when the stack is deleted.

cards.front: Determine whether anyone modified CloudFormation stack resources manually via the console. What?

choices.why: Preview updates, not detect manual edits.
Compares live resources to the template.

cards.front: Developers prefer defining infrastructure in TypeScript/Python rather than YAML. What?

choices.why: Web-app automation, not IaC language choice.

Prevent accidental updates to a critical resource during CloudFormation stack updates. What?
Reuse a common VPC pattern across many CloudFormation templates. What?
